title: GenRecon: Bridging Generative Priors for Multi-View 3D Scene Reconstruction
claim: A sparse set of input views is turned into one complete, editable, high-fidelity scene asset that supports downstream applications.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, big arrow from inputs to central top-down mesh
description: Three rounded gray panels read left to right. The left panel, titled 'RGB Input', stacks three indoor photos (living room, bedroom, kitchen) separated by vertical dots to show a variable number of views. A large dark gray arrow points to the wide center panel, 'PBR Mesh Reconstruction'. That panel shows a top-down textured mesh of a multi-room apartment, tilted diagonally in the middle. Four corner insets surround it, each a photo-like render with a diagonal split into a rainbow normal-map or material overlay, which suggests PBR channels and geometry. The right panel, 'Relighting', has three renders of the same living room under neutral, dim and saturated red/green/blue lighting. The eye goes first to the central floorplan-like mesh.
caption: GenRecon. Given a sparse set of RGB images of an indoor scene (left), our method reconstructs a complete, high-fidelity PBR mesh (center) by formulating scene reconstruction as conditional 3D generation over overlapping spatial chunks. The recovered mesh with material properties enables realistic relighting and editing in standard rendering pipelines (right).
abstract: We introduce a new approach to high-fidelity 3D scene reconstruction from multi-view RGB images that tightly couples reconstruction with a strong generative 3D prior. We cast scene reconstruction as conditional 3D generation over a set of spatially-localized, overlapping chunks that together tile the scene, scaling generation to large scene extents. Crucially, we inherit the fidelity and completeness of state-of-the-art generative shape models -- we use Trellis.2 as an example -- which we generalize to the scene level. To this end, we propose a projection-based conditioning mechanism that lifts posed multi-view image features into a coherent 3D representation aligned with the generative model, independent of view ordering and spatially anchored to the scene, yielding high-fidelity, multi-view consistent generated geometry. This enables lifting the strong object-level prior of Trellis.2 to multi-view, scene-scale generation, producing faithful, editable PBR mesh reconstructions of indoor environments. As a result, we obtain high-fidelity results that outperform cutting-edge reconstruction methods by 16%.
